title: Feedback Tapestry: Proposal Lanes for Optimize
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working synthesis of customer feedback related to Redwood Optimize (cost/perf toolkit) collected Feb–Apr 2026 across support tickets, CSM interviews, and partner calls. Goal: convert recurring asks into 3 prioritized proposal lanes (Quick Wins, Medium Effort, Strategic Bets) with suggested owner, acceptance criteria, and initial rollout plan.

How this was compiled:
- Sources: 42 support threads (tags: optimize, batching, quant), 6 CS interviews (enterprise accounts), 2 partner technical reviews, Slack channel #optimize-feedback history (Feb–Apr).
- Method: grouped raw asks into themes, counted frequency, surface customer quotes, scored by impact (estimated cost savings / user pain), and feasibility (infra + product effort).

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
Customers want clearer, automated guidance and safer guardrails from Optimize: automated batching presets per model/route, a lightweight quantization sanity-checker, and an integratable scoreboard that maps config -> estimated cost and delta in latency/quality. Most asks are low-to-medium effort but high impact in terms of reducing token spend and support cycles.

Topline themes and representative asks:
1) Automated config recommendations (frequency: 18 mentions)
   - "We run 6 models and don't know the right batch size per model—can Optimize suggest presets?" (SaaS startup, 3B monthly tokens)
   - Requests: per-model batch presets, sequence-length-aware defaults, recommended caching TTLs

2) Quantization/precision safety checks (frequency: 12 mentions)
   - "Quantization saves $$ but hallucinations spiked in one test—how to know when it's safe?" (Enterprise legal search)
   - Requests: pre-deploy QC checks, quick A/B eval harness, human-readable risk summary

3) Cost/latency impact scoreboard (frequency: 14 mentions)
   - "Before we change config we want to see expected delta in latency and cost for our workload" (Platform team)
   - Requests: estimator UI that shows % cost change + 95th latency impact, per-route, with confidence band

4) Rollout primitives for Optimize suggestions (frequency: 9 mentions)
   - Canary/beta toggles for batching/quant changes, automatic fallback if quality regresses

5) Better telemetry hooks and alerting (frequency: 8 mentions)
   - Prometheus / Datadog friendly metrics for Optimize decisions + drift alerts when workload distributions change

Prioritized proposal lanes:
A. Quick Wins (0.5–3 sprints)
   1. Batching presets UI + API endpoint (owner: Marco)
      - Short description: Add a lightweight UI card on Optimize Routes that recommends 3 presets: low-latency, balanced, max-throughput. Also expose an API to fetch preset params for programmatic rollout.
      - Acceptance criteria (AC): presets appear in UI for 80% of routes; API returns sensible defaults for selected model families; 2 pilot customers accept presets and see >=10% cost reduction in 2 weeks.
      - Risks: presets might be suboptimal for atypical sequence-length distributions. Mitigation: show a sticky note about sequence length and add an override toggle.

   2. Quick quantization checklist (owner: Samantha)
      - Short description: Preflight checklist that runs a small suite (50 prompts) comparing baseline vs quantized model and surfaces delta in key metrics (exact-match, perplexity proxy).
      - AC: checklist runs in <10 minutes for typical model; generates human-readable risk summary; rollout doc created.

B. Medium Effort (2–5 sprints)
   1. Cost/Latency Estimator (owner: Diego)
      - Short description: Backend estimator that uses route token distributions and model perf profiles to estimate cost and latency delta for a proposed config change.
      - AC: estimator within 15% of observed cost delta in 3 pilot routes; UI shows confidence interval; linked to rollout diff view.
      - Dependencies: runtime perf profiles, job to periodically compute route token distributions (SRE/Infra ticket).

   2. Canary + Auto-Fallback for Optimize changes (owner: Priya)
      - Short description: Lightweight canary that applies new batching/quant config to X% traffic with a monitoring window; if quality or latency regress beyond threshold, automatically revert.
      - AC: 3 configurable thresholds (latency, error-rate, quality-threshold) and automated rollback tested on staging.

C. Strategic Bets (3+ months / partnership)
   1. Continuous Quality Regression Detector (owner: TBD)
      - Short description: Integrate eval set monitoring so Optimize watches selected prompts and detects regressions tied to config changes (and model updates). Can link to alerting and rollout automation.
      - AC: regression alerts for seeded regressions in controlled tests; links to PR/Ticket creation flow for ops.
      - Note: needs research on robust, small eval sets per customer. Consider offering as paid add-on for enterprise.

Customer quotes and signal snippets (raw):
- "If Optimize could give me a one-click estimate of cost change I'd try more aggressive batching." — Platform lead, fintech
- "We wasted 2 weeks trying different quant configs; a small checklist would have saved us hours." — CS contact, legal search
- "A scoreboard that shows confidence intervals would make it easier to justify changes to our compliance team." — Infra manager, healthcare

Quick data points to justify prioritization:
- 18/56 feedback items referenced automated recommendations (32% of sample)
- Pilot partner estimate: average token cost reduction potential 12–25% when using batching + caching
- Support load: ~4 engineering hours per week spent triaging Optimize-related config questions across two CS reps

Design notes and UX sketch (rough):
- UI card in Optimize Routes: top shows estimated cost delta (sparkline), center has 3 presets with tooltips, bottom has a "simulate" button that opens estimator overlay.
- Preflight checklist: modal with 6 quick checks (sanity, small eval, latency smoke, cache TTL recommendation, failmode guidance, doc link).

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the right sample size and prompt selection logic for the quantization checklist? (action: research/AML)
- Do we need to surface model-variant tradeoffs (e.g., fp16 vs 4-bit) or keep it generic? (action: runtime team sync)
- How to price a Continuous Quality Regression feature? subscription vs usage? (action: GTM)

Proposed next steps (next 4 weeks):
1) Align with runtime/infra on what perf profiles we can expose (owner: Diego) — target: decision by 2026-04-23
2) Build Quick Wins tickets: batching presets API + checklist (owners: Marco, Samantha) — spike + acceptance criteria by 2026-04-30
3) Recruit 2 pilot customers for presets/estimator (owner: Priya + CSM) — commit by 2026-05-07
4) Create experiment framework for canary/rollback (owner: SRE liaison) — draft by 2026-05-14

Implementation notes and rough effort estimates:
- Batching presets: 2 dev sprints + 1 designer + 1 SRE (can ship as UI + API).
- Quant checklist: 1 sprint + small AML work to pick representative prompts.
- Estimator: 3–4 sprints including backend job to collate token distributions and a lightweight ML model to produce confidence intervals.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Presets could be misapplied and lead to customer regressions. Mitigation: default to 'balanced' and require explicit opt-in for aggressive presets; add warning and easy rollback button.
- Risk: Estimator predictions inaccurate for highly skewed workloads. Mitigation: show confidence band and require a short simulation run for high-risk routes.

Notes to self and rough meeting transcript snippets:
- "We should avoid overpromising—show a 5–25% band, not exact numbers" — Marco 2026-04-06
- "Enterprise legal wants exportable evidence of no QA regressions" — CSM Sam 2026-04-08

Appendix: sample support tickets (IDs and paraphrased)
- INF-4821: customer reports increased hallucinations after quantizing; asks for checklist.
- OPT-923: feature request for estimator in Console; includes sample logs.

Decision log (for reviewers):
- Recommended priority: Quick Wins -> presets + checklist. Rationale: high signal frequency and low infra dependency.
- Medium: estimator because higher backend dependency; still high impact.

Reviewer asks (please comment inline):
- Are we comfortable exposing estimator predictions before we have a simulation run? (yes/no)
- Suggested metric to trigger auto-fallback? (pct latency increase / absolute ms threshold)

-- end of working doc --

Privacy note: contains paraphrases of customer quotes and ticket summaries; do not redistribute externally without CSM approval.
